newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China unveils list of nominees for 1997 HK body.
newsitem.headline: China unveils list of nominees for 1997 HK body.

text.p: Chinese officials issued a list of over 5,000 people nominated to sit on a body that will pick Hong Kong's future leaders after Britain departs next year, but denied they had acted under pressure to be more accountable.

The Preparatory Committee published the list late on Wednesday of 5,791 people nominated to sit on the 400-member body which will choose the first post-handover chief executive and a provisional legislature.

"It will give people the impression that the whole process is transparent and open," Fih Fei, a senior official with the China-controlled Preparatory Committee's secretariat, told Reuters on Thursday.
But Fih denied China had bowed to pressure to make the process appear more accountable.
"We listen to the public," Fih said. "But to say that we were under pressure isn't true. We never said the list of nominations would not be made public."
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997.

Beijing has vowed to scrap the territory's elected legislature in retaliation for democratic reforms implemented by colonial Governor Chris Patten. A provisional legislature will be set up as a stop-gap measure until new elections are called.
Fih said the membership of the Selection Committee would be announced in early November after final shortlisting.
"The published list is only a preliminary one," she said. "We will carefully study each of the applications to see if they meet the requirements."

The published list included politicians as well as former government officials, among them Sir David Akers-Jones, at one time Britain's highest ranking civil servant in the territory under the colonial governor.
The government banned senior civil servants from joining the Selection Committee, a decision which one union had attempted unsuccessfully to overturn in court.

The one-month nomination period closed in the middle of this month. There are more than 3,000 nominations for 100 of the Selection Committee seats that are reserved for grassroots representatives, making this the most competitive of four categories of seat.

China has assured Hong Kong that its own people, and not Beijing officials, will lead the territory of 6.2 million people after the change of flag and that its capitalist way of life will be preserved for at least 50 years.
